unit.title: Public Goods, Taxes, and Community Choices

lesson.title: Real Jobs That Taxes Help Pay For
lesson.subject: social-studies

contentBlocks.text: You've learned about public goods and taxes. Today: meet the real jobs that taxes help pay for!

Some jobs are paid for by taxes because they serve the whole community, not just one customer: firefighters, public-school teachers, librarians at a public library, and people who keep public parks clean. This connects to last week's idea that communities need many different specialized jobs — these are jobs specialized to serve everyone, paid for together. Pick one of these four jobs and explain how it helps the whole community, not just one person.
You just connected real community jobs to taxes and public goods! Tomorrow we'll practice a real community decision together.

objectives: Name real jobs that are funded by taxes because they serve the whole community
Explain how one tax-funded job helps the community as a whole, not just one individual
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review this week's public-goods and taxes lessons.
2. Introduce the four example tax-funded jobs, connecting back to last week's specialization idea.
3. Have the child pick one job and explain how it serves everyone.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's community-decision activity.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just the firefighter example, the clearest 'serves everyone equally' case
Ready for more: ask the child to name a job NOT paid for by taxes (like a toy-store worker) and explain the difference
This lesson is a good moment to revisit K Social Studies' community-helpers content through a new, economics-aware lens
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an open-ended explanation activity — check that the child picks one of the four jobs and correctly explains it serves the whole community rather than one individual customer.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses the C3 Framework's Economics and Civics dimensions together at a Grade 2 level, connecting tax-funded jobs to community-wide benefit.
